The buggy revision uses floating RR[a,b,...] domains, causing explosive rounding errors that produce huge Floats (e.g. around 1e200). The fix converts to an exact QQ[a,b,...] domain before inversion. Reproduce by running the two newly-introduced pytest cases in sympy/matrices/tests/test_matrixbase.py on the buggy commit; they should fail because the result contains Floats with magnitude >= 1e3 and/or the exact identity check fails.

Observe the test output: on the buggy commit, the Float-max assertion fails (max(abs(f) for f in Mi.atoms(Float)) >= 1e3) and the equality assertion may also fail.
strategy.expected_buggy_behavior: Both new tests fail. test_inverse_symbolic_float_issue_26821 reports that max(abs(f) for f in Mi.atoms(Float)) is >= 1e3 (and possibly that (M*Mi - eye(7)).applyfunc(cancel) != zeros(7)). test_matrix_exponential_issue_26821 reports max(abs(f) for f in Me.atoms(Float)) >= 1e3 or that (Me.diff(t) - M*Me).applyfunc(cancel) != zeros(7).
strategy.expected_fixed_behavior: Once the fix is applied, both tests pass: Matrix.inv() and (t*M).exp() compute the exact matrix result with floats bounded in magnitude (< 1e3) and satisfy the corresponding exact identities.
strategy.success_criterion: At the buggy commit 66c229001b7d1a02870e96ce4b0c92cb5fe1b6c9, running the two selected pytest tests reports at least one failure in each test (the Float-max bound and/or the residual identity assertions). After applying PR #26822 (commit b65c687588bab22db54c7984231cf72be115fb34), the same tests pass on the same environment, confirming the reproduction targets the reported numerical bug.
risks_or_ambiguities: The PR test diff's inverse test constructs a 7x7 symbolic matrix with float coefficients and uses the @slow decorator only on the exponential test; running pytest normally includes slow tests by default.
The buggy behaviour may be platform/domain dependent because it stems from floating-point rounding in RR; the failure should be visible but exact numerical values may vary.
The evidence reports CI matrix uses Python 3.9-3.12 and several optional deps; the reproduction may need a recent mpmath if running the exp test on a matrix with floats.

The test assertions check only that max(abs(f) for f in Mi.atoms(Float)) < 1e3 and the residual; the exact huge Float values are not pinned, so no fixed numerical constant can be asserted beyond the test bound.
The full matrix expressions are long; copying them into a runner is error-prone. Prefer using the actual test file from the PR.
